info.title: Consola Cloud API
info.description: Who is signed in, their workspaces, and what each workspace holds. Sign-in itself is Better Auth’s, under /api/auth, and is not described here.

GitHubCallbackResult.description: How a Connect ended, as the callback names it in the web app’s `?github=`.

Me.description: Who is signed in, and their session’s active workspace.

icon.description: The icon the workspace wears, by the desktop app’s ids; null for none, which shows its initial.

canManage.description: Whether the person may change how the workspace looks (an owner or admin).

MyWorkspace.description: A workspace as one of its members sees it.

WorkspaceIconChange.description: An icon from the desktop app’s set, or null to take the icon off.

WorkspaceMember.description: A member of a workspace, as its other members see them.

InvalidWorkspace.description: Every problem, in the order the rules name them.

NewWorkspace.description: A name (trimmed, at most 64 characters) and a slug of lowercase letters and digits with single dashes between (at most 48). The workspace is made in the deployment’s region, which no request names.

canManage.description: Whether the caller may make, rename and delete teams, and choose their members.

TeamList.description: The teams the caller sees: every team for owners and admins, the ones they are in for a member.

first.description: Whether it is the workspace's first team, which every new member joins and which is never deleted.

memberIds.description: Its members’ ids, in the order they joined it: only people who are members of the workspace now.

InvalidTeam.description: Every problem with the name, at once.

TeamName.description: A name (trimmed, 1 to 64 characters, no control characters), unique in the workspace whatever its case.

FactoryList.description: The factories the caller sees, by name: every factory for owners and admins, the factories of the teams they are in for a member.

latestVersion.description: Its latest version's number: 1 until its files are first saved, and one more with each save.

updatedAt.description: When its latest version was saved, as an ISO 8601 time.

FactorySource.description: Where the factory's files come from: `stored`, saved in Consola. A GitHub repository comes later.

InvalidFactory.description: Every problem with the name, at once.

NewFactory.description: A name (trimmed, 1 to 64 characters, no control characters), unique in the workspace whatever its case, and the id of the team that owns it.

FactoryWithFiles.description: A factory, and its latest version with its files.

savedAt.description: When it was saved, as an ISO 8601 time.

savedBy.description: The id of the person who saved it.

FactoryVersion.description: One version of a factory's files, as saved.

path.description: Its path inside the factory's folder: `factory.yml`, `automations/<name>.yaml`, `agents/<name>.md`, `skills/<name>/…`.

name.description: Its new name (trimmed, 1 to 64 characters, no control characters), unique in the workspace whatever its case.

teamId.description: The id of the team that owns it from now on.

FactoryChange.description: What changes, at least one of the two: both at once is one change, made whole or not at all. Its files and where they come from are not changed here.

SavedFactoryVersion.description: The version saved, and what to know about it.

FactoryNotice.description: Something the factory schema says about the files that refuses nothing, such as a folder a later slice reads.

InvalidFiles.description: Files that fail the factory schema: every problem, each naming its file. Nothing is saved.

file.description: The file the problem is in; absent for a problem with the set as a whole.

path.description: Where in the file, as a dotted path into its document (`automations[0].mode`); empty for the whole file.

automation.description: The automation the problem belongs to, when it has a name.

cause.description: The file (or skill's folder) whose own problems this one only shows through: a step's agent, an agent's skill.

FactoryIssue.description: A problem with the files, as the factory schema words it.

VersionMoved.description: The latest version is no longer `baseVersion`: someone saved since. Nothing is saved.

baseVersion.description: The version the files were edited from, which must still be the latest: a save never undoes one it did not see.

files.description: Every file of the new version (at most 500, 8 MB in all): a file left out is not in it.
Its files, by path inside a factory's folder, to merge into a factory through the ordinary save.

FactoryTemplate.description: Ready-made factory files a person can start from, such as an agent team.

nextCursor.description: The next page's `cursor`; null on the last page.

facets.description: What the filters offer, whatever the query's filters: the factories and teams the caller sees, by name, and the automations their runs ran, children's included.

RunList.description: Top-level runs (none a request started) the caller sees, newest first: every run for owners and admins, the runs of their teams’ factories for a member.

title.description: A request: its item's title, else its text's first line; an automation run: its item's title, else its automation's name. At most 120 characters, on one line.

waitingOn.description: What a waiting run waits on; set exactly while it is `waiting`.

factory.description: Its factory, and the version of it the run executed.

teamId.description: The team that owns the run's factory now.

automation.description: The automation's name; null exactly for a request.

parentId.description: The request that started it, on an automation run one did.

triggerDetail.description: What the trigger was: the event's name (`pull_request.opened`), the cron schedule, or the poll's check.

startedBy.description: The id of the person who started it, who may no longer be a member; null for a run no person started.

runner.description: Which runner ran it: `cloud` for now.

current.description: The id of the first step running or waiting.

progress.description: An automation run's steps; null for a request.

children.description: The automation runs a request started, by phase; null otherwise.

costUsd.description: The CLI's estimate, in dollars; a request's counts its runs too. Null while none was reported.

createdAt.description: When it was made, as an ISO 8601 time.

startedAt.description: When it started working, as an ISO 8601 time.

finishedAt.description: When it ended, as an ISO 8601 time.

updatedAt.description: When its runner last recorded it, as an ISO 8601 time.

RunKind.description: A `request`, whose one step is its factory’s orchestrator, or an `automation` run, with steps.

RunStatus.description: A run's status. The set only grows.

Phase.description: Consola's grouping of a run's status, which the list filters and counts by: `active` (queued, running, waiting on a run), `needs-you` (needs approval, waiting on a person, or a request at work one of whose runs needs someone), `completed`, `failed` (failed, expired) and `stopped` (cancelled, rejected).

RunTrigger.description: How a run was started: a schedule (`cron`), an event, a poll, or someone’s act (`manual`). A run a request started is `manual`.

title.description: Written by its author: text, never markup.

RunItem.description: The pull request or issue a run is about.

PhaseCounts.description: How many runs are in each phase.

version.description: The version an answer applies to: the run's factory version.

reason.description: Why it asks, in one plain sentence.

team.description: Who may answer: anyone on the factory's owning team.

mayAnswer.description: Whether the caller is on that team.

will.description: What approving lets run, as the definition writes it: each command and each agent step. Empty for a request.

by.description: The id of the person who answered.

answer.description: The answer for this version: the first one given.

RunApproval.description: A run's request to be approved: present while the run needs approval, and once answered. Consola records the answer; the run's runner acts on it.

ApprovalAnswer.description: Approve or dismiss a run waiting for approval, at the version the caller was shown: the run's factory version.

parent.description: The request that started it, which whoever sees the run sees.

steps.description: An automation run's steps, in file order; a request's one `orchestrator` step.

text.description: The request as the person gave it. Untrusted (it may be a pasted ticket): show it as plain text only.

spent.description: Its turns and its runs, as the engine sums them; runs it started.

question.description: The orchestrator's open question: when it was asked, and its deadline. Its text is not in Consola.

request.description: A request's own facts; null for an automation run.

children.description: The automation runs a request started, in the order it started them.

conversation.description: The cloud session holding a request's conversation with its orchestrator, once there is one: an agent run's. Null for an automation run.

id.description: The step's id in its automation, or `orchestrator`.

attempt.description: From 1: the nth time it ran in this run.

agent.description: The agent file it names (`agents/<name>.md`), if any.

outputs.description: The latest execution's outputs, checked against their types.

artifacts.description: The documents it wrote; empty when none.

deniedTools.description: Tools a turn was refused, each once, in first-seen order.

turn.description: An agent step's turns, summed over its latest attempt.

command.description: A command step's result; null for an agent step, or before it ran.

previous.description: Its earlier attempts in this run, oldest first; empty when none.

reminded.description: Whether Consola reminded the agent to finish its step.

truncated.description: Whether more came before what is kept.

output.description: The end of what its latest attempt printed, as its runner last sent it: at most 16 KiB of each. Untrusted: show it as plain text.

StepStatus.description: A step's status. The set only grows.

prompt.description: The prompt as written: a template, never rendered.

outputs.description: The outputs it declares, each type in words (`one of: a, b`).

file.description: The file it is written in, in the factory.

version.description: The factory version it was read from.

range.description: The step's lines in its run's `source.text`; null when they are not known.

StepDefinition.description: What a step was asked, as its automation's file says at the factory version the run executed.

LineRange.description: Lines of a file, from 1, both ends included.

path.description: The file the automation is written in: `automations/<name>.yaml`, or `factory.yml`.

version.description: The factory version the run executed.

text.description: The whole file, at that version.

detail.description: The cron schedule, the event(s), or the poll's check, as written.

appliesTo.description: Which items a run on demand takes; empty when none.

RunSource.description: The file behind an automation run, at the factory version it executed, and the automation's own lines in it (`range`: the whole file for `automations/<name>.yaml`). Null for a request (its orchestrator has no file in Consola yet), and when that version does not define the automation.

items.description: The agent CLI the session runs.

CloudSessionOptions.description: What the workspace's connected runner offers: where a session can start, and with what.

personId.description: The id of the person who started it, the only one who sees it; null for an agent run, which every member of the workspace sees.

harness.description: The agent CLI the session runs.

status.description: `starting` goes to `running` or `failed`, and `running` to `stopped` or `failed`; `stopped` and `failed` are ends.

title.description: What the runner named it; for an agent run, Consola's own title (`<automation> · <owner/name>#<number> <title>`), which the runner never replaces.

hostUrl.description: The origin the session's host listens on, once the runner reported it.

error.description: The message the runner reported for a failure (its provider’s or its start script’s), shown as it came. A failed session has this or `errorCode`, never both.

errorCode.description: A failure Consola decided itself, which the web app words: the runner restarted, could not be reached, or failed without a message; for an agent run, also no runner connected (`runner_unavailable`), its repository or harness not offered, or a start Consola could not compose (`agent_run_invalid`).

runnerId.description: The runner the start was handed to; null for an agent run no runner took, which ended as it was recorded.

createdAt.description: When it was started, in epoch seconds.

endedAt.description: When it ended, in epoch seconds; null while it lives.

origin.description: What started an agent run; null for a person's session.

agentRun.description: The runner's last report of an agent run; null until it sent one.

CloudSession.description: A cloud session: a sandbox the workspace's runner runs for a person, or an agent run an automation started, which nobody types into.

automation.description: The automation that fired, by name.

agent.description: The agent that takes the first turn: the automation's, by default the orchestrator.

headSha.description: The commit the run checks out.

item.description: The GitHub pull request the event was about.

CloudSessionOrigin.description: What started an agent run: an automation of a factory's agent team, on an item.

summary.description: The first agent's last message, as the runner reported it.

agents.description: The agents the first agent dispatched.

AgentRunReport.description: The runner's last report of an agent run, as it sent it.

repository.description: One the runner offers, as `owner/name`; its name may not start with a dot.

harness.description: The agent CLI the session runs.

NewCloudSession.description: Exactly these two fields: a body naming anything else, a workspace above all, is refused.

pass.description: The session pass, a compact JWS signed with Consola's own pass key, which the session's host checks.

hostUrl.description: The origin the session's host listens on.

expiresAt.description: When the pass expires, in epoch seconds: its `exp`.

canManage.description: Whether the person may connect and disconnect: an owner or admin.

configured.description: Whether this server has the GitHub App’s settings.

Connections.description: What the workspace is connected to.

settingsUrl.description: Where on GitHub its repositories are chosen, and it is uninstalled.

GitHubConnection.description: A GitHub App installation the workspace holds.

GitHubAccount.description: The GitHub account, an organisation or a person, the app is installed on.

GitHubRepositories.description: What GitHub says the installation covers now: its repositories, `gone` when GitHub no longer has the installation (uninstalled or suspended there), or `unavailable` when GitHub did not say. Asked of GitHub each time, never stored.

GitHubWebhookPong.description: GitHub’s ping, as a webhook is set up: recorded for no workspace.

GitHubWebhookRecorded.description: The event is recorded for the workspace that holds its installation.

post.summary: Make a blank factory, owned by a team

patch.summary: Rename a factory, or move it to another team
patch.description: Whoever sees the factory may rename it. Moving it needs the caller to see the team it moves to as well: owners and admins any team, a member a team they are in. Its versions stay as they are.

403.description: The person is not a member of the workspace their session has active, or no longer (`not_a_member`), or the change did not come from the web app (`bad_origin`).

404.description: The caller sees no such factory (`factory_not_found`), or no such team to move it to (`team_not_found`): none, or one a member is not in.

409.description: Another factory of the workspace has the name, in any case (`name_taken`). Or: The session has no workspace active (`no_active_workspace`), or another than the page shows (`workspace_switched`): another tab switched it. Loading the page again is the fix.

415.description: The body is not JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).

get.summary: The top-level runs the caller sees, newest first
get.description: A request is one run; the automation runs it started are not listed here but in its own answer. Filters combine; the values of one filter are alternatives.

post.summary: Approve or dismiss a run that waits for approval
post.description: Anyone on the run's factory's owning team may answer, whatever their workspace role, and the first answer for a version is the one kept. Consola records it and does not change the run: its runner acts on it.

get.summary: Where GitHub sends a person back after installing the app
get.description: The GitHub App’s callback URL, reached by a browser redirect from GitHub with `state`, `code`, `installation_id`, `setup_action` or `error`. It never answers JSON: it always redirects to the web app’s Settings, on its Connections page, with how the Connect ended in `?github=`: one of `connected`, `already_connected`, `requested`, `cancelled`, `bad_state`, `expired`, `not_allowed`, `code_refused`, `not_installer`, `not_account_admin`, `taken`, `invalid`, `unavailable`, `not_configured`, `signed_out`.

post.summary: Receive one of the GitHub App’s webhook deliveries
post.description: The GitHub App’s webhook URL. GitHub calls it, with no session and no Origin, so it is outside the origin check. The body is GitHub’s event payload as JSON, read as raw bytes and checked against `X-Hub-Signature-256` (HMAC-SHA256 under the app’s webhook secret, compared in constant time) before anything else is read; `X-GitHub-Event` names the event and `X-GitHub-Delivery` is GitHub’s id of the delivery, which it keeps when it sends a delivery again. The event is recorded for the workspace that holds its installation, once per delivery id, and an event recorded now starts the agent runs its factories’ teams fire.

400.description: Signed, but a header or the body is not what GitHub sends.

401.description: No `X-Hub-Signature-256`, or not GitHub’s signature over this body.

409.description: The workspace had this delivery already: sent again, or replayed. Nothing changed.

413.description: Over the 26214400 bytes (25 MB) GitHub puts in a delivery at most.

422.description: Dropped: the event came through an installation no workspace holds, or through none.

503.description: This server has no webhook secret (`GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `webhooks_not_configured`), or its database did not answer (`unavailable`): GitHub’s Redeliver sends it again.
